synopsis: The glossary identifies SCALEXIO as a real-time HIL system and VEOS as PC-based virtual ECU simulation; Chapter 11 groups SCALEXIO, VEOS and AURELION as commercial replay and HIL tools supporting ECU execution with virtual sensors [f16034, f8363, f9219, f8639]. AURELION and SIMPHERA integrate with the dSPACE ecosystem, and the booklet describes the combined tools as a strong route from software-in-the-loop to hardware-in-the-loop testing [f8448, f8999, f8640]. That route requires sensor- and ECU-specific engineering: camera video, radar targets, Ethernet streams and raw stimulation are materially different injection problems [f8641]. J1939 emulation is reported possible per ISO/TS 21815-2, but the listed evidence for these tools is on-road only, leaving off-road applicability unsubstantiated by that evidence [f9221, f9220]. Both the glossary and Chapter 11 place the dSPACE combination among highest-cost example chains, yet neither a public price nor a full-system price was found [f16166, f9303, f9222, f8642].

relations.note: Both list the dSPACE combination among highest-cost commercial platform chains.
The glossary distinguishes SCALEXIO's real-time HIL role from VEOS's PC-based simulation role.
ECU and HIL execution with virtual sensors supports the proposed SIL-to-HIL route.
Integration across the dSPACE ecosystem supports the SIL-to-HIL route.
The interface listing adds an OSI-compatible chain and explicit SIL/HIL interfaces.
Implementing the SIL-to-HIL route requires sensor- and ECU-specific injection engineering.
Virtual-sensor execution involves materially different injection methods for different sensor types.
The full-system price gap specifies a missing cost scope within the public-price gap.
The example locates these commercial tools within a highest-cost validation and orchestration chain.
